slot_note: wave 3 (oviya1301), seed ET12 (analytical_tasks/07_data_extraction_conformation): the world (a health department certifying whether a program bent the curve on a cause of death), the decision and the quantity only
niche: cause-of-death classification error on death certificates, measured by a medical examiner's record reviews, under a county overdose initiative's certified outcome
stakeholder_role: the county public health department's epidemiology program manager

spine.file: state vital records death certificate extract, county residents, 2019 to 2026
spine.entity: one death of a county resident
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a state vital records death file with multiple-cause ICD-10 codes)

world.geography: United States (an unnamed state, an invented county)

driver: A register's count of one class is wrong in both directions, and the records wrongly placed in the class come from a neighbouring pool that stays level while the class shrinks; reviews of sampled records show the measurement's sensitivity and specificity steady across periods while its net error and predictive values move with the class's size, so each period's count is corrected by the steady error rates, and the count as filed, or corrected by a net ratio or predictive values measured when the class was larger, understates the class's fall.
driver_concrete: Tamsworth County's death certificates miss about one opioid overdose death in eight and certify as opioid overdoses some stimulant and other drug deaths with an incidental opioid listed, a pool that did not fall when opioid deaths did; the medical examiner's record reviews of 2022 and 2025 show the certificates' sensitivity and specificity steady while their positive predictive value and net error moved, so each year's true count is the certified count corrected by sensitivity and specificity, and the certified counts, or counts corrected by the reviews' net ratio or predictive values, put 2026 short of the 20 per cent fall below the 2021 to 2023 average that the corrected count meets.
stump: The default path declines to certify because it reads the certified opioid overdose deaths as the count and finds 2026 short of a 20 per cent fall below the 2021 to 2023 average; correcting each year for the certificates' sensitivity and specificity, which the reviews show steady, puts 2026 more than 20 per cent below and certifies the target met.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the death files, applies the case definition and adjusts each year with the 2022 review's correction (its net ratio, or its positive and negative predictive values) still finds 2026 short of a 20 per cent fall and declines to certify.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the true number of residents who died of an opioid overdose, estimated from a register whose classification error a gold-standard review measured; administrative-data quality's own analysis (net against gross classification error, a count corrected by the error rates that stay steady) decides, and with another field's nouns (a retailer's sales, a plant's output) there is no register misclassification measured by review and the task stops reading the same.
notes: draw 2026-10-13: the seed's ICD-9 to ICD-10 comparability bridge is not used (a documented-break bridge, the family of task453's level shift); its world, decision and quantity are kept
